messages:
Tomáš Novák: doing a quick review of the perf-canary regression triage runbook before we roll it into oncall training. request: can we add a super explicit “what to do first” checklist at the top? folks are going to get paged at 2am and the current doc starts a bit too deep.

Sean Gallagher: +1. the doc is good but needs a 60-second path. also want training plan spelled out (who/when, dry run vs live). we’ll get fewer “where do i click” pages.

Talia Benson: i can coordinate a 30-min training slot next week w/ SRE + runtime. but i need the minimal checklist content to put in the agenda + send ahead.

Rafael Mendes: for training, would be good to cover: (1) alert payload anatomy, (2) how to use the dashboard links, (3) when to page Runtime vs open ticket. plus “don’t touch customer traffic” reminder.

Allison Grant: runbook review comment: please align the checklist steps with the actual dashboard naming + panel IDs in Grafana. right now it says “open perf dashboard” but there are 3.

Tomáš Novák: yep. right now the first section says “confirm signal quality” but doesn’t tell you how. can we do a top block like:
- open dashboard link
- verify sample count
- compare against baseline
- check deploy annotation
- verify it’s not a suppression window
- decide severity + route
?

Nadia Rahman: from metrics side: please explicitly call out minimum sample size + time window. we’ve already seen false positives when the canary runner restarts and you get like 6 samples in the window.

Logan Wright: also call out the label dimensions that matter (model/region/gpu_sku/runtime_build/scheduler_mode). responders keep looking at “all gpu” and it hides a single sku regression.

Omar El-Sayed: can add a “quick sanity check” step: confirm canary tag is present (`source=perf-canary`) and runtime_build label isn’t “unknown”. if labels are missing, it’s telemetry/instrumentation, not perf.

Sean Gallagher: agree. also want a hard “DO NOT” list:
- don’t crank canary rate
- don’t restart production serving pods to “test”
- don’t change scheduler flags outside of rollback procedure

Tomáš Novák: ok drafting checklist. pls critique:

Tomáš Novák: 
```
Perf Canary Regression: What to do first (2–5 min)
1) Open the alert’s Grafana link (model+region panel pre-filtered).
2) Confirm signal quality
   - Window: last 30m vs baseline panel
   - Samples: >= N requests in window (see panel “canary_request_count”)
   - Check for runner restart / gaps (panel “canary_runner_heartbeat”)
3) Identify the slice
   - Compare by gpu_sku and runtime_build (use dashboard quick filters)
   - Check scheduler_mode is pinned (expected: “pinned_stable”) for canary
4) Correlate with deploys
   - Look at deploy annotations in the panel (runtime_version/git_sha)
   - If regression starts within 15m of deploy: likely deploy-related
5) Verify it’s not expected noise
   - Ensure not in a maintenance/suppression window
   - Check “warmup/cold cache” note: first 10m after rollout can be noisy
6) Triage routing
   - If sustained regression + deploy-correlated: page Runtime (kernel/scheduling)
   - If labeling/data issue: ping Telemetry (no page) + file ticket
   - If unclear: page SRE secondary for second set of eyes
7) Mitigation (only if confirmed)
   - Prefer rollback of runtime build / disable canary slice per runbook
   - Do not change customer routing without incident lead
```

Allison Grant: this is close. tweaks:
- step 2: specify exact metric names as they appear in dashboards (or link to the “Metrics” tab). “canary_runner_heartbeat” might not be on v1 dashboard.
- step 3: “pinned_stable” — is that the canonical value? i think runtime emits `scheduler_mode=pinned` and a separate `scheduler_profile=stable` (?)

Omar El-Sayed: correct, label is `scheduler_mode=pinned` and we tag `scheduler_pin_profile=stable_v1` for now. (we can rename later but docs should match reality).

Logan Wright: for step 2, we do have `perf_canary_requests_total` broken out by model/region. heartbeat is `perf_canary_runner_last_success_ts` (gauge). i’ll paste exact strings here once i confirm.

Nadia Rahman: also include the “p95 computation sanity check”:
- if p95 jumps but p50 is flat + request_count low => suspicious
- if p95 + p50 both move and tokens/sec drops => real regression more likely

Sean Gallagher: routing language: we should avoid “page Runtime” as default. propose:
- Sev2 page Runtime only if > threshold AND > 2 windows AND deploy correlated
- otherwise create ticket + post in #eng-runtime with dashboard link
this matches the alert policy doc.

Rafael Mendes: +1. also for training: i can run a “fake page” drill with incident-bot posting into #eng-oncall. we can walk through the checklist live.

Incident Bot: (simulated) perf-canary regression detected: model=rw-open-13b region=eu-west metric=p95_latency regression=+18% baseline=7d_median window=30m
Links: grafana://perf-canary?model=rw-open-13b&region=eu-west | runbook://eng-sre/runbooks/perf-canary

Tomáš Novák: this is actually perfect for training. we can screen share and do the steps.

Talia Benson: ok training plan proposal:
- 25 min session (SRE oncall + runtime oncall optional)
- 10 min: alert payload + severity expectations
- 10 min: live drill using simulated alert + checklist
- 5 min: escalation paths + where to file tuning feedback
can we do Tue 11am PT?

Sean Gallagher: works for me. pls send calendar + link the runbook draft. tomas, incorporate the routing nuance + metric name corrections.

Logan Wright: confirmed metric strings in dashboards:
- request count: `perf_canary_requests_total`
- runner health: `perf_canary_runner_last_success_ts` (panel labeled “Runner last success”)
- latency: `perf_canary_latency_ms` (p50/p95 panels)
- throughput: `perf_canary_tokens_per_sec`
labels: model, region, gpu_sku, runtime_build, scheduler_mode, scheduler_pin_profile, streaming

Allison Grant: great. last note: please keep the checklist short in the runbook, but link to a “deep dive” section below. otherwise it becomes a wall.

Tomáš Novák: ack. i’ll add the checklist block at top, then “if still unsure, continue” below. will post updated runbook link in channel for final review.

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: once updated, we’ll treat checklist as required for v1 launch. also add a note: “if regression is only on one gpu_sku, include that in the ticket title.” helps a lot.

Rafael Mendes: and in the incident-bot payload, i’ll make sure gpu_sku + runtime_build are included in the top-level fields (not buried). we got that request in the other thread too.

Tomáš Novák: cool. i’ll loop back here w/ final text + training agenda doc.
